milestone.title: mp-flow skill — cross-role orchestration, 12-stage timeline, role-binding table, hand-off contract

intent.outcome: After this ships, the `mp-flow` skill is the cross-role orchestration reference for the full milestone lifecycle — from writing the spec to closing the review rounds. Any agent (coordinator or runner) loads it as the meta-skill that lays out the 12-stage timeline (Draft → Groom → Specify → Approve → Claim & execute → Self-review → Complete → External review → Remediate → Re-review → Document → Hand off) and binds each stage to the role that owns it. Stages 1-4 (Draft / Groom / Specify / Approve) are the coordinator's domain; stages 5-7 (Claim / Execute / Self-review / Complete) are the runner's; stages 8-10 (External review / Remediate / Re-review) iterate as a loop; stages 11-12 (Document / Hand off) wrap the cycle. The skill carries a single canonical procedure, the role-binding table, the hand-off contract between coordinator and runner, the `mp-flow-lint` content gate (asserts the 12 stage headings via `templates/skills/mp-flow/stages.toml`), the single-source invariant (back-link to `master-planner`), and the L5 cross-link (`docs/code-review-lessons.md`). The actual role-specific deep-dives ship as separate skills: `mp-coordinator` (M121) for planning + reviewing + spec-co-design, `mp-runner` (M122) for executing + fixing, and `mp-handoff` (M123) for the four hand-off points between roles.

problem.description: M98's original `mp-flow` skill was monolithic: a single 12-AC artifact covering all stages of the execute → review → remediate → document → commit cycle as one content block. The user's two-agent / four-role architecture (coordinator = planning + reviewing, runner = executing + fixing) requires the role-specific deep-dives to live in their own skills, not conflated with the cross-role timeline. Beyond the role split, the user's revised model (2026-07-07) extends mp-flow beyond the post-approval lifecycle: mp-flow now starts at "writing the milestone" (Draft) and ends at "ready for execution" (Approve). This is the coordinator's domain; the AC + scope defined here are the key inputs to the downstream code review (stages 8 + 10). So mp-flow covers the full 12-stage lifecycle (Draft → ... → Hand off), and the four hand-off points between coordinator and runner domain boundaries are encoded as M123. Additionally, the M98 monolithic skill's design decision (the 'schema-capped at 2 digits' rationale) referenced a constraint that no longer exists (3ebaee4 + dc6052e widening; the historical marker now lives in `crates/mp/MIGRATIONS.md`, see M119 AC-08); that historical marker should be archived, not propagated. M98 (the original monolithic skill) and M99 (the lesson-pattern skill) are archived once M120 lands and the role-specific skills (M121, M122) ship.

in_scope: `templates/skills/mp-flow/SKILL.md` (the cross-role flow) — the 12-stage timeline with concrete `mp` commands per stage (1 Draft, 2 Groom, 3 Specify, 4 Approve, 5 Claim & execute, 6 Self-review, 7 Complete, 8 External review, 9 Remediate, 10 Re-review, 11 Document, 12 Hand off), the role-binding table (coordinator owns 1-4, 8, 10, 11, 12; runner owns 5, 6, 7, 9), the 8-9-10 review loop annotation, the hand-off contract summary (deep-dive in M123), the single-source invariant (back-link to `master-planner`), the L5 cross-link, and pointers to the role-specific skills.

`templates/skills/mp-flow/flow-stages.md` (the deep-dive per-stage checklist) — extracted from M98's `flow-stages.md` spec; covers the gotchas surfaced during M93/M94/M95 (gate parity, dry-run honesty, op-arg up-front validation, no-op semantics) and the new stages 1-4 (Draft / Groom / Specify / Approve) checklists for the coordinator's spec-authoring domain.

`templates/skills/mp-flow/stages.toml` (the structured stage manifest) — a TOML file enumerating the 12 stages with their `mp` commands and required role-binding. Replaces the brittle free-text grep on stage headings.
`make mp-flow-lint` content gate — parses `stages.toml` and asserts `SKILL.md` has the matching `## <stage-name>` sections with the required `mp` commands. Failure stops the build.

Back-link to `master-planner`: `templates/skills/master-planner/SKILL.md` gets a one-line `## See also` section pointing at `mp-flow` (single-source invariant AC-05). M120 owns this cross-link as the natural party that establishes the cross-skill references; the master-planner side is one-line and ships with M120.

Worked-example artifact (optional): running the skill against M93 or M94 produces a committed transcript at `docs/mp-flow-walkthrough-M<M>.md` containing the 12 stage headings. M98 already specifies this; M120 picks it up unchanged and updates the stage count.

Skill explicitly forbids same-session self-review and cites `docs/code-review-lessons.md` L5 as the reason. The two-round review pattern (runner self-reviews in stage 6, coordinator externally reviews in stage 8) is the role-binding protocol that M120 surfaces; the deep-dive lives in `mp-coordinator` (M121) for stages 8 + 10 and `mp-runner` (M122) for stage 6; the hand-off protocol lives in `mp-handoff` (M123).

8-stage → 12-stage expansion: M120 owns the expansion from the original 8-stage model (M98) to the current 12-stage model. The expansion adds stages 1-4 (coordinator domain) at the front of the timeline; stages 5-7 (runner domain) and 8-10 (review loop) replace the prior monolithic execute/review/remediate block; stages 11-12 wrap the cycle. The expansion is documented as a design_decision so future readers of M98 understand the lineage.
out_of_scope: Role-specific deep-dive content for the coordinator (planning sub-mode, reviewing sub-mode, spec-co-design sub-mode) — M121.
Role-specific deep-dive content for the runner (executing sub-mode, fixing sub-mode) — M122.
The hand-off protocol deep-dive (what data, what session-boundary, what evidence, four hand-off points) — M123.
Replacing `master-planner` (M120 back-links; doesn't duplicate). The master-planner back-link is one line in M120; the master-planner SKILL.md itself is unchanged content-wise.
Replacing `spec-grill` (coordinator's adversarial sub-mode; lives in M121's spec).
The lesson-pattern library in `docs/code-review-lessons.md` — owned by the coordinator's reviewing sub-mode (M121). M120 surfaces L5; the patterns themselves live elsewhere.
The four hand-off protocol contracts (planner → runner, runner → coordinator self-review, coordinator → runner with findings, runner → coordinator re-review) — M123.

design_decisions.area: Why a separate cross-role skill (mp-flow) instead of folding the role-binding into mp-coordinator and mp-runner:
design_decisions.choice: mp-flow is the canonical reference that any agent loads first, before role-specific skills. The role-binding table and hand-off contract are not role-specific — they describe how coordinator and runner interact. Folding them into either role would force the other role to read the partner's skill just to know the hand-off contract. A separate cross-role skill keeps the timeline authoritative in one place.
design_decisions.rationale: Single source of truth for the lifecycle timeline. The role-specific skills (M121, M122) reference the stages they own; mp-flow references the roles that own each stage. The cross-link is symmetric and avoids the 'who owns the hand-off contract?' ambiguity.

design_decisions.choice: M98 was archived as part of the M119 → M120 sequence closure (M119 ships the registry, M120 ships the cross-role orchestration, M121/M122 ship role-specific deep-dives, M123 ships the hand-off protocol). M98's monolithic content has been split: install/registry surface → M119; cross-role timeline → M120 (now expanded to 12 stages per the user's 2026-07-07 model revision); role-specific deep-dive → M121 (coordinator) + M122 (runner). M98's design_decisions and intent.outcome are preserved in git history; the historical markers (e.g., the 'schema-capped at 2 digits' rationale) now live in `crates/mp/MIGRATIONS.md` (M119 AC-08). The M120 expansion is forward-compatible with the original M98 scope — anyone using mp-flow for the post-approval stages (5-12) gets the same content plus 4 new coordinator-domain stages at the front.
design_decisions.rationale: M98's monolithic content conflated three things: install/registry surface (now M119), cross-role timeline (now M120), and role-specific deep-dive (now M121 + M122). The split is the same one the user identified in the broader two-agent / four-role discussion; M120 is the formalization of that split for the mp-flow content side.

design_decisions.choice: SKILL.md cites `docs/code-review-lessons.md` L5 ('same-session self-review is unreliable') by name and links the L5 lesson to the role-binding table. The hand-off protocol deep-dive (how to actually split a session across the L5 boundary) lives in `mp-handoff` (M123). M120 surfaces the L5 lesson at a high level only — it doesn't re-document the hand-off protocol.
design_decisions.rationale: M120 is the timeline. M123 is the protocol. L5 is the rationale. Three different documents, three different scopes. The cross-link keeps them coherent without duplicating content.

design_decisions.choice: mp-flow now starts at "writing the milestone" (Draft, stage 1) and ends at "ready for execution" (Approve, stage 4), then continues through the runner's execute (5-7) and review loop (8-10) and the coordinator's wrap-up (11-12). The original 8-stage model (M98) covered stages 5-12 — execute through hand off — but assumed a ready milestone was already in hand. The user's revised model (2026-07-07) extends mp-flow's scope to include the coordinator's spec-authoring domain (stages 1-4) because the AC and scope defined there are the key inputs to the downstream code review (stages 8 + 10). So the 12-stage timeline has a clear split: stages 1-4 are coordinator domain (the work the runner will review later), stages 5-7 are runner domain, stages 8-10 iterate as a loop, stages 11-12 wrap. M121 owns the coordinator's role-specific deep-dive for stages 1-4 + 8 + 10; M122 owns the runner's deep-dive for stages 5-7 + 9; M123 owns the hand-off protocol between them.
design_decisions.rationale: The 12-stage model was driven by the user 2026-07-07 clarification: mp-flow covers the full lifecycle from "starting to write" through "completing the review rounds", with the coordinator owning the spec-authoring domain. The expansion is structurally simple (4 new stages at the front of the timeline) but semantically important — it makes explicit that AC + scope are coordinator outputs and runner inputs, which is the foundation for the code review protocol.

findings.description: AC-01 verification command is wrong. The spec says: "cargo test -p raul --lib mp_flow_lint && grep -c "^## " templates/skills/mp-flow/SKILL.md | awk "{ exit (\$1 >= 12) ? 0 : 1 }"". There is no Rust test named mp_flow_lint in the raul or mp crate (verified: cargo test -p raul --lib mp_flow_lint returns "0 passed, 65 filtered out"; cargo test -p mp --lib mp_flow similarly). The actual gate is make mp-flow-lint which runs scripts/mp_flow_lint.py — a Python script that parses stages.toml and asserts each stage has a `## <name>` section in SKILL.md with the listed commands. Remediation: amend AC-01 description to reference `make mp-flow-lint` (the actual gate) instead of the non-existent Rust test.
findings.author: external:review-m120
